name: Congenital High Airway Obstruction Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Prenatal Ultrasound Diagnostic Criteria for CHAOS

criteria.description: Bilateral enlarged, echogenic lungs on prenatal ultrasound
Dilated trachea or main bronchi distal to obstruction
Flattened or inverted diaphragm on imaging
Presence of fetal ascites or hydrops fetalis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral enlarged echogenic lungs with dilated airway and inverted diaphragm on prenatal imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily prenatal via ultrasound and MRI; postnatal diagnosis is rare due to lethality.

searchTerms: both lungs appear large and bright on ultrasound
bilateral lung enlargement with increased echogenicity

pathognomonic.symptomName: Airway obstruction at or above the larynx
searchTerms: blocked airway at or above voice box

common.symptomName: Fetal hydrops (ascites, pleural effusion, skin edema)
searchTerms: fluid buildup in fetus tissues and cavities
hydrops fetalis with ascites and edema

common.notes: Excess amniotic fluid due to impaired swallowing

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent fetal breathing movements
searchTerms: reduced or no fetal breathing movements
missing or blocked windpipe or voice box

occasional.notes: Heart displaced due to lung enlargement

searchTerms: excess amniotic fluid causing early labor
too much amniotic fluid triggering early delivery

rare.symptomName: Associated congenital anomalies (e.g. congenital diaphragmatic hernia)

imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing bilateral enlarged echogenic lungs
MRI confirming airway obstruction and lung enlargement
Flattened or inverted diaphragm on imaging
Dilated trachea or main bronchi distal to obstruction
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases
Some associations with syndromic conditions involving airway malformations
other: Fetal echocardiography showing cardiac compression or displacement
Postmortem findings confirm airway atresia or stenosis

distinguishingFeatures: Localized overinflation of a lung lobe rather than bilateral lung enlargement
No airway obstruction at or above the larynx
Fluid accumulation limited to pleural space
No bilateral lung enlargement or inverted diaphragm
Herniation of abdominal contents into thorax
Displacement of heart and lungs but not bilateral lung enlargement

redFlags: Severe airway obstruction incompatible with postnatal ventilation
Development of fetal hydrops indicating cardiac failure
Rapidly progressive polyhydramnios causing preterm labor
references: Nicolaides KH, et al. Prenatal diagnosis of congenital high airway obstruction syndrome. Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol. 1994.
Lee W, et al. Congenital high airway obstruction syndrome: prenatal diagnosis and management. Prenat Diagn. 2019.
Orphanet: Congenital high airway obstruction syndrome (ORPHA:700286).
